remediation.issue: Several examples use generic SELECT star queries before showing optimized forms.
remediation.suggestion: Keep the examples, but label unsafe or slow examples clearly so users do not copy them into production unchanged.

content.value_statement: Slow queries increase application latency and database costs. This skill guides indexing, EXPLAIN review, and query rewrites for faster SQL performance.
actual_capabilities: Explains common EXPLAIN plan signals such as sequential scans, index scans, join types, costs, and row estimates.
Suggests index strategies for equality filters, range filters, composite keys, partial indexes, and covering indexes.
Identifies common SQL performance anti-patterns, including SELECT star, N+1 queries, large offsets, and correlated subqueries.
Recommends query rewrites for joins, pagination, aggregation, subqueries, batch inserts, and batch updates.
Provides validation steps using query plans, slow query logs, database statistics, and maintenance commands.
limitations: It does not connect to databases or collect live query metrics by itself.
Recommendations must be tested against the actual schema, data volume, and workload.
Examples focus on PostgreSQL and general SQL, with limited MySQL-specific coverage.
It does not replace security review for permissions, sensitive data, or production change control.

use_cases.title: Tune a Slow Endpoint
use_cases.description: Review a slow query, interpret its plan, and choose indexes or rewrites that reduce response time.

use_cases.title: Review Database Indexes
use_cases.description: Compare query patterns with existing indexes and identify missing, redundant, or poorly ordered indexes.

use_cases.title: Plan Scaling Work
use_cases.description: Prioritize high-impact SQL changes before traffic growth or a major product launch.

prompt_templates.title: Review One Query
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of a single slow query.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the SQL optimization patterns skill. Review this slow query and explain the most likely bottlenecks in plain language: [paste query].

prompt_templates.title: Interpret an EXPLAIN Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate plan analysis with query context.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the SQL optimization patterns skill. Analyze this EXPLAIN output and suggest indexes or query rewrites: [paste query and plan].

prompt_templates.title: Fix N Plus One Access
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the SQL optimization patterns skill. Identify N+1 query risks in this data access flow and propose batch loading or joins: [paste flow].

prompt_templates.title: Design a Tuning Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workload optimization across several queries.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the SQL optimization patterns skill. Build a prioritized tuning plan for these queries, schema notes, data volumes, and latency goals: [paste details].

output_examples.input: A slow user lookup query with a filter on email and no useful index.
output_examples.output: The skill would explain why a full table scan is likely, recommend an email index, and ask for an EXPLAIN plan to confirm.

output_examples.input: An API endpoint loads users, then loads orders once for each user.
output_examples.output: The skill would identify the N+1 pattern and suggest a join or batch query with grouped results.

output_examples.input: A reporting query uses a large offset for pagination on a growing table.
output_examples.output: The skill would recommend cursor-based pagination and an index that matches the sort order.

best_practices: Share the query, relevant schema, current indexes, row counts, and EXPLAIN output when asking for help.
Validate every recommended change with before-and-after query plans and realistic data volume.
Consider write overhead, storage cost, and maintenance impact before adding indexes.
anti_patterns: Do not add indexes without matching them to real query predicates and sort orders.
Do not optimize only from syntax when execution plans and production metrics are available.
Do not run destructive or locking maintenance commands in production without a reviewed rollout plan.

faq.question: Does this skill connect to my database?
faq.answer: No. It provides analysis and recommendations from information you provide.

faq.question: Which databases does it support?
faq.answer: It is strongest for PostgreSQL and general SQL patterns. Some examples mention MySQL behavior.

faq.question: Can it read EXPLAIN plans?
faq.answer: Yes. It can help interpret plan operators, row estimates, costs, timing, and index usage.

faq.question: Will every suggested index improve performance?
faq.answer: No. Index value depends on data distribution, workload, write volume, and query frequency.

faq.question: Can it fix ORM performance issues?
faq.answer: It can identify common ORM issues such as N+1 queries and suggest joins, preloading, or batch loading.

faq.question: Should I run examples directly in production?
faq.answer: No. Test changes in a safe environment and follow normal database change controls.
